summary: The measurement path is geometrically defensible for the claim. The implementation distinguishes projected 2D centerline length, endpoint Z span, sampled Z coverage, projection-plus-Z length, calibrated centroid-path tortuosity, observed-slice mask volume, and sampled ROI volume. The new apparent body-width definition is orientation-tested, uses a deterministic representative plane, preserves explicitly labelled legacy fields, and returns missing values when support is insufficient. Focused manual execution confirmed anisotropic 3D path scaling, non-interpolated gapped-track volume, and unavailable-width behavior. These measurements characterize segmented masks and reconstructed tracks; they do not establish anatomical organ volume, PSF-corrected chromatin width, biological mechanism, or a genotype effect.

findings.title: Measurements describe segmented-image geometry, not direct biological anatomy
findings.impact: Apparent body width, mask volume, projection-plus-Z length, centroid-path tortuosity, effective thickness, and sampled ROI volume can vary with segmentation, PSF, optical sampling, tracking, and acquisition boundaries. They cannot alone establish chromatin dimensions, anatomical organ volume, biological mechanism, or a group effect.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12836-12848 labels 3D length as a projection-plus-Z estimate, volume as summed mask pixels, and effective thickness as a PSF-sensitive proxy.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12944-12948 states that width depends on optical resolution, PSF, focus, and mask boundaries.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12929-12934 states sampled ROI volume is not anatomical tissue or whole-organ volume.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:74-76 states that the reported two-specimen values are not a genotype inference.
findings.recommendation: Retain these limitations beside tables and figures and base between-group inference on specimen-level measurements with matched acquisition conditions.

limitations: The audit scope prohibited running a full image stack.
